title: A yearly retreat
tomorrow: does God care which road you walk to pray?

lines: NO LEISURE SO MUCH AS TO EAT.
cards: The out-of-office reply is set, the laptop is closed, and then the phone lights up. Mark tells a version of that. Jesus' friends come back from a hard stretch of work, so busy “they had no leisure so much as to eat.”
He says, “Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while.” They get in a boat. And the crowd runs along the shore and gets there first.
The retreat is over before it starts. So why does Jesus let it go?

teach.b: Mark says what Jesus saw when he stepped out of the boat: he “was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd.” So he teaches them, and by evening the crowd is fed.
Here's the strange part, worth telling a friend: the rest wasn't canceled.
It was moved. A few verses later, once everyone has gone home, Mark says “he departed into a mountain to pray.” Jesus keeps coming back to it.
Mark tells of him “rising up a great while before day” and going out to a solitary place to pray. Luke puts it in one line: “And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed.”
A desert place, in these stories, means somewhere lonely, out of the traffic. A sabbath and daily prayer are short pauses.
A retreat is a longer one: a day, a weekend, set apart to be quiet with God. Christians keep it in different ways. Some stay at a monastery or retreat house and join its rhythm of prayer.
Some go with a church group, or meet a guide each day. Some take a quiet day at home, phone off, a Bible open.
So the puzzle's answer is a plan: the crowd will always find the boat, so time apart gets put somewhere on purpose, and kept again when it slips.

how: Christians make retreats in many ways: a stay at a monastery or retreat house, a guided retreat with a director, a church group weekend, or a quiet day at home with the phone off and a Bible open.

o: a church meeting to plan the coming year's budget
a step back from belief after a hard season
time set apart, a day or more, to be quiet with God

s: in Mark, Jesus sends the crowd away so his friends can rest
he's moved with compassion and teaches them. the rest comes later, on a mountain.
in the Gospels, Jesus himself goes off alone to pray
a solitary place before day; the wilderness; a mountain.
a retreat has to mean a monastery far from home
some Christians take a quiet day at home with the phone off and a Bible open.

games.q: you blocked off Saturday as a quiet day. Friday night a neighbor asks for help moving. what fits Mark's story?
o: say no. time with God comes before anyone else.
help, and put the quiet day on a new date.
help, and drop the idea. retreats never work out.
games.why: Jesus is moved with compassion and teaches the crowd, then goes up a mountain to pray once they've gone. the rest is moved, not canceled.

practice: Open a calendar, on paper or on your phone, and find one day in the coming months that could be quiet. Mark it, even if it's only a morning, and give it a name you'll recognize.
Then spend the rest of the sit as a small rehearsal of that day.

wordCard.voice: A yearly retreat. Time set apart, a day or more, to be quiet with God, out of the coming and going.

orig.note: Greek: a deserted, lonely place; the desert place of Mark 6:31.

carryVoice: The line to keep: come apart awhile, and if the crowd finds the boat, keep it later. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
